subject: Film & Cinema
title: Cross-Cutting: Parallel Tension
description: A fast breakdown of Cross-Cutting: Parallel Tension for builders.

hook.text: Cutting between two scenes happening at once creates a tension neither scene has alone.

buildup.text: Cross-cutting — also called parallel editing — shows simultaneous actions building to a collision.

discovery.text: Griffith pioneered it. Nolan perfected it — Inception cross-cuts four timelines at once.

twist.text: Cross-cutting works because the brain naturally compares and anticipates convergence.

climax.text: It's cinema's most reliable way to generate urgency without a single line of dialogue.

punchline.text: Two stories told together create a third feeling.

quiz.question: What film cross-cuts between four simultaneous timelines?
